summary: Yanling Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA from Fo Guang University (attested 2012) under the supervision of Yongdong Shi, and also studied under Hsing Yun.

Yannick Laurent works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He held posts as Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and Dr. at the University of Munich, both attested in 2026.
Yanpei (1917–1996) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Taixu around 1934–1937 and as a student under Yinshun around 1941–1945.
Yao Wang (1928–2015) was a scholar in Tibetology who studied under Gongkar Tulku. He served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.
Yao-ming Tsai works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. After earning a PhD from the University of California by 1997, he became Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
Yaping Dou is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2010) under the supervision of Xue Yu.

Komarovski specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at several Tibetan institutes, under multiple traditional teachers, and at the University of Virginia. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis and a post at University of Nebraska-Lincoln (attested 2011–2015).

Yaroslav Vasilkov (born 1943) is an Indologist who studied at St. Petersburg University (circa 1961–1967). He held posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences around 1967 and at Saint Petersburg State University, including its Faculty of Philosophy.

Yasuaki Nara (1929–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Kogen Mizuno, and at the University of Calcutta. He served as professor emeritus at Komazawa University.

Yasuhiko Nagano (born 1946) is a Tibetologist and linguist educated at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley (PhD). He served as professor and professor emeritus at the National Museum of Ethnology, among other administrative roles.
Yasuhiko Sueki (born 1952) is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1972 to 1978 and became an emeritus professor at Komazawa University around 2018.

Yasuhiro Okazaki is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned a PhD at Hiroshima University under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono. He held teaching posts at Chiyoda, Kabe, and Hiroshima Prefectural Takamiya high schools.

Yasuhiro Sueki (born 1952) is a Buddhist studies scholar who undertook short-term study at Tübingen University Library (1990–1991). He held positions at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, serving as deputy director.

Yasuhiro Tsuchiyama (born 1950) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, he serves as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Yasuhiro Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004) and held a research post at Koyasan University (attested 2004).

Yasuhiro Yamazaki (1929–2025) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Koyasan University (circa 1950–1954). He later served as an assistant professor at Shuchiin University (1966–2000) and as a professor at Koyasan University (circa 1977–2000).

Yasuke Ikari (born 1940) is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Chicago (PhD). He spent much of his academic career at Kyoto University, rising to professor in 1989 and professor emeritus in 2004.

Yasuko Kojima is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested in 2026, she holds lecturer positions at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yasumasa Sekine (born 1949) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology educated at Tokyo Institute of Technology and SOAS. He held faculty posts at Gakushuin Women's Junior College, University of Tsukuba, Japan Women's University, and Kwansei Gakuin University.

Yasunori Ejima (1939–1999) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his degrees at the University of Tokyo and researched at Göttingen. He served as assistant professor at Nagaoka University of Technology and later as professor at Tokyo.
